items.h: Treylon Burks (foot) limited in practice Wednesday
items.s: Treylon Burks was limited in practice on Wednesday. Burks was limited out of the bye week with a foot injury. He is in line for an expanded role if he is healthy with Terry McLaurin out for the season.

items.h: Limited by foot injury Wednesday
items.s: Burks (foot) was limited in Wednesday's practice. Burks was injured toward the end of Washington's Week 6 loss to the 49ers two Monday nights ago, but he was at least able to get in a limited session coming out of the bye week. With Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year, Burks is expected to take on a larger role, along with rookie Antonio Williams, behind Stefon Diggs (hand) at wide receiver.

items.h: Treylon Burks in Line for Uptick in Playing Time in Washington
items.s: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks should be in line for an uptick in playing time going forward after Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury in the Week 6 loss to the San Francisco 49ers last Monday night. Burks played 55.2% of the offensive snaps against the 49ers and caught four of his six targets for a season-high 66 yards in the 23-17 loss. The 26-year-old's receptions and targets were also season highs in the same game that McLaurin went down with an injury, which is not a coincidence. Veteran Stefon Diggs should operate as quarterback Jayden Daniels' go-to passing-game target, but both Burks and rookie Antonio Williams should have added responsibilities,…

items.h: Treylon Burks an Interesting Waiver Target After Teammate's Injury
items.s: Washington Commanders wide receiver Treylon Burks had his best game of the season in the Monday night loss to the San Francisco 49ers, and it was not a coincidence that it came in the same game in which Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury. Burks played 55% of the offensive snaps and caught four of his six targets for 66 yards in the 23-17 loss on the road in the Bay Area. The 26-year-old former 18th overall pick by the Tennessee Titans in 2022 from Arkansas now has nine grabs on the year in five games for 152 yards and two touchdowns, and with McLaurin now out for the rest of the season, he should have a regular role in three-wide sets alongside Stefon Diggs and rookie…

items.h: Season-best marks in catches, yards Monday
items.s: Burks finished with four receptions for 66 yards on six targets in Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers. The reception, yardage and target totals were all season-best totals for Burks, whose heightened involvement in the passing game may have been a byproduct of No. 1 wideout Terry McLaurin (knee) exiting the game late in the first quarter. Though Burks didn't see a major spike in playing time compared to prior weeks -- he was on the field for 37 of 67 offensive snaps (55.2 percent) -- he should be able to maintain a regular role in three-receiver sets alongside Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams, with McLaurin expected to miss time and potentially even being sidelined for the rest of the season.

items.h: Treylon Burks goes for 66 yards in Week 6
items.s: Treylon Burks caught four of his six targets for 66 yards in a 23-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 6. Burks finished second on the Commanders in receiving yards behind only Chig Okonkwo. The veteran receiver saw an expanded role after Terry McLaurin suffered a knee injury in the first half and was carted off the field. Burks will have some flex appeal in Week 8 after his Week 7 bye, assuming McLaurin can't play.

items.h: Ready for Week 6
items.s: Burks (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's game in San Francisco. Burks practiced in a limited capacity during the entirety of Week 6 prep due to a shoulder issue, but it won't stop him from being available Monday. Fellow WR Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is listed as questionable, and if he's inhibited or sidelined this week, Burks will stand to benefit in the Commanders' passing game. In four contests this season, Burks has notched five catches (on 11 targets) for 86 yards and two touchdowns.

items.h: Still limited Friday
items.s: Burks (shoulder) remained limited in Friday's practice. Stefon Diggs (hamstring) upgraded to limited after being DNP on Thursday, and Terry McLaurin got a veteran's rest day after returning from his hamstring injury last Sunday. Burks caught two of five targets for 26 yards in last Sunday's 27-27 tie with the Giants.

items.h: Treylon Burks (shoulder) listed as limited Thursday
items.s: Treylon Burks (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant at practice on Thursday. A shoulder injury left Burks limited at practice on Thursday. It doesn't look like it will leave him sidelined for Week 6, however, and he will again be primed for more work than usual if Stefon Diggs (hamstring) misses another game for Washington.

items.h: Tending to shoulder issue
items.s: Burks was limited at Thursday's practice due to a shoulder injury. After being a healthy scratch in Week 1, Burks has been active and increased his snap share in each of the ensuing four contests, a span in which he combined for a 5-86-2 line on 11 targets. While Burks and No. 1 WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring) both opened Week 6 prep with capped sessions, Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was held out entirely Thursday. If Diggs requires another absence Monday at San Francisco and Burks is active, the latter again should be a regular option for QB Jayden Daniels in the passing game.

items.h: Burks caught two passes on five targets for 16 yards during Sunday's 27-27 tie with the Giants.
items.s: Burks saw a season-high five targets during Sunday's game, which was second-most on the Commanders behind Chig Okonkwo (six). Burks only logged two catches, but his season was a 13-yard pass late in overtime that set the Commanders up well within field-goal range, only for Jayden Daniels to mismanage the clock to end the game on a tie. Burks has a 5-86-2 receiving line on 10 targets over his last three games, though his scoring floor would take a considerable hit if Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is cleared to play in the Commanders' Week 6 road game against the 49ers on Monday.

items.h: Burks caught one of three targets for a 47-yard touchdown in Sunday's 30-13 loss to the Colts.
items.s: With Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive, Burks saw increased snaps in the Commanders' wideout rotation that also involved Stefon Diggs, Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams. Burks saw the fewest targets of the four and made the most of his one grab, breaking off a 47-yard score in the third quarter. If McLaurin continues to miss time, Burks should see rotational playing time at wideout, but he's not currently a playable fantasy option.

items.h: Burks failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 37-20 loss to the Cowboys.
items.s: After being inactive in the season opener against the Eagles, Burks played 21 offensive snaps against Dallas as the fifth receiver behind Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, Dyami Brown and rookie Antonio Williams. Burks doesn't have any fantasy value in redraft formats at the moment.

items.h: Burks (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
items.s: Burks appeared in eight of the Commanders' final nine games of the 2025 regular season after being released by the Titans in October. However, the 2022 first-rounder will join Luke McCaffrey (coach's decision) in street clothes Sunday, with the Commanders opting for five active wide receivers for game day. Burks' next chance to play is Week 2 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.h: Burks (foot) returned to Commanders practice Saturday, Zach Selby of the Commanders' official site reports.
items.s: Burks missed Thursday's practice due to a sore foot, but he wasn't held out of action long. That's good news for the 2022 first-round draft pick, as he has an opportunity during training camp to compete for a major role in the offense. Antonio Williams and Luke McCaffrey are among the other players jostling for the No. 2 WR role behind Terry McLaurin in an unsettled Washington receiver corps.

items.h: Burks missed Thursday's practice with foot soreness, Ben Standig of Big 100 Washington D.C. reports.
items.s: The 2022 first-round pick is part of what seems to be an open competition for WR roles behind locked-in No. 1 Terry McLaurin. Rumors connect Washington with multiple veteran wideouts, but the current depth chart gives Burks a real shot at a top-three role, competing against the likes of Antonio Williams, Luke McCaffrey, Dyami Brown, Jaylin Lane and Van Jefferson.

items.h: The Commanders re-signed Burks to a one-year contract worth up to $4 million Friday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: After some injury-plagued seasons in Tennessee, Burks signed with Washington back in October and appeared in eight regular-season games for the Commanders last season. He reeled in 10 of 22 targets for 130 yards and one touchdown on 60 percent of the offensive snaps across the second half of the season. The Commanders' wide-receiver depth chart is wide open behind Terry McLaurin, as Deebo Samuel is ticketed for free agency next week.

items.h: Burks caught two of four targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 24-17 win over the Eagles.
items.s: Burks worked as Washington's No. 3 receiver throughout much of the second half of the season, ultimately catching just 10 of 22 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in eight games. The 2022 first-round pick is scheduled for unrestricted free agency this offseason.

items.h: Burks (illness) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest in Philadelphia, Nicki Jhabvala of The Washington Post reports.
items.s: Burks showed up Thursday as a non-participant due to an illness, but his return to all activity one day later sets him up to be available to the Commanders offense this weekend. While working with No. 3 QB Josh Johnson last Thursday against the Cowboys, Burks played 91 percent of the snaps but was targeted just twice, hauling in one of them for 11 yards. Burks likely will have a similar role Sunday working alongside top WRs Terry McLaurin and Deebo Samuel and Johnson under center in place of Marcus Mariota (right hand/quadriceps).

items.h: Burks (illness) did not practice Thursday.
items.s: Burks wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, an indication that his illness is a new development. Unless he's able to resume practicing in full Friday, it appears that Burks will be assigned an injury designation for Washington's season finale against the Eagles on Sunday, for which third-string quarterback Josh Johnson is trending toward another start.

items.h: Burks secured one of two targets for one yard during Thursday's 30-23 loss to the Cowboys.
items.s: Burks also attempted one pass on a trick play near the end of the third quarter, but he was sacked. Though Burks has found limited success as a deep threat in Washington, he was unable to get anything going with No. 3 quarterback Josh Johnson under center on Christmas Day. It will be beneficial to Burks' limited fantasy appeal if Marcus Mariota (hand) manages to return in time for Washington's regular-season finale against the Eagles in Week 18.

items.h: Burks tallied two catches on five targets for 30 yards Saturday in a loss to the Eagles.
items.s: Burks (45 offensive snaps), Terry McLaurin (45) and Deebo Samuel (44) logged nearly equal workloads, and Burks actually led the Commanders in targets. However, he finished third among the trio in yardage, with most of his production coming on a 24-yard catch on the first play of the third quarter. Of note, starting QB Marcus Mariota -- who was filling in for Jayden Daniels (elbow), who is out for the season -- didn't finish Saturday's contest after suffering a hand injury in the second half, and Josh Johnson had to take over following Mariota's departure. Washington's offense would likely be…

items.h: Burks didn't catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 29-21 win over the Giants.
items.s: The 2022 first-round pick from Arkansas has now gone without a catch in each of the Commanders' last two games. Since joining the active roster before the Week 9 loss to the Seahawks, Burks has caught five of 11 targets for 77 yards and a touchdown. He's expected to remain a depth option in Washington's wide-receiver corps in the Week 16 matchup against the Eagles.

items.h: Burks failed to reel in his only target in Sunday's 31-0 loss to the Vikings.
items.s: Burks and the rest of Washington's offense were limited greatly, producing just 215 total yards in the blowout loss. The wide receiver logged 19 snaps on offense, which ranked fourth at his position behind Terry McLaurin (32), Noah Brown (32) and Deebo Samuel (27) in Week 14. Burks will look to get more involved in the team's Week 15 matchup with the Giants on the road.

items.h: Burks caught one of four targets for a five-yard touchdown in Sunday night's 27-26 overtime loss to the Broncos.
items.s: With Terry McLaurin not playing full snaps in his return from a quadriceps injury, Burks played 66 percent of the Commanders' offensive snaps against Denver, even though he was also returning from a broken finger. Burks' four targets were still a distant fourth on the team, but he made his lone catch count with a spectacular one-handed touchdown grab in the corner of the end zone. It was Burks' first touchdown catch since Week 13 of his 2022 rookie season with the Titans. With McLaurin and Deebo Samuel healthy, Burks carries minimal fantasy value.

items.h: Burks (finger) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
items.s: Burks sat out the Commanders' last game Week 11 due to a finger injury that required surgery, but with the benefit of a Week 12 bye, he followed up back-to-back limited practices to open Week 13 prep with a full session Friday, setting him up to suit up this weekend. With top WR Terry McLaurin (quadriceps) back in the lineup and Deebo Samuel also on hand, Burks will be in the mix for snaps and targets behind them along with Jaylin Lane and Chris Moore.

items.h: Burks (finger) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Burks' finger injury prevented him from suiting up Week 11, and he's still managing the issue coming out of Washington's bye. He may have to log full practice reps Friday in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Broncos. Wideouts Terry McLaurin (quad) and Noah Brown (knee, IR) have both also retaken the practice field for Washington, meaning Burks could find himself relegated to a depth role even if he's able to return Week 13.

items.h: Burks (finger) was a limited participant in practice Wednesday.
items.s: Burks briefly became Washington's No. 3 receiver, but he missed Week 11 with a finger injury and now comes out of a Week 12 bye with more competition for playing time. Terry McLaurin (quad) and Noah Brown (knee) both returned to practice this week.

items.h: Burks has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins due to a finger injury.
items.s: Burks was signed to the Commanders' active roster this past Tuesday and made an impact during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Lions, when he led Washington with 58 receiving yards on three catches. However, the 2022 first-rounder came out of that contest with a finger injury, which was severe enough for him to undergo surgery Monday, per Adam Schefter of ESPN. Burks will miss Sunday's game in Spain, but the finger injury isn't considered a long-term issue, meaning he could be cleared to return following the Commanders' Week 12 bye.

items.h: Burks secured all three of his targets for 58 yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Detroit.
items.s: Burks led Washington in terms of receiving yards against Detroit with Marcus Mariota under center and Terry McLaurin (quadriceps) sidelined, though he was outpaced by both Deebo Samuel and tight end Zach Ertz in terms of targets. As Burks was signed to the active roster in advance of Sunday's contest, he'll get another chance to contribute on offense as the Commanders travel to Madrid in Week 11 to take on the Dolphins. If McLaurin is unavailable again versus Miami, Burks could be considered as an emergency pivot option at wide receiver in deeper fantasy formats.

items.h: Washington signed Burks to its active roster Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: The Commanders are dealing with injuries to multiple notable contributors at wide receiver, so it's not a huge surprise to see them bring up reinforcements at the position. Burks logged 32 offensive snaps in his first game with Washington in Week 9, bringing in his only target for 14 yards.

items.h: Burks reverted to Washington's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.s: After joining the Commanders' practice squad in mid-October, Burks got his first elevation ahead of Sunday's loss to Seattle. He logged a pretty hefty workload with 33 of 65 offensive snaps, finishing fourth among Washington's wideouts. Burks caught his only target for 14 yards in the contest and also played two snaps on special teams. Terry McLaurin (quadriceps) missed the matchup and isn't expected to return in Week 10, per Nicki Jhabvala of The Washington Post, and Luke McCaffrey fractured his collarbone Sunday, so there's a good chance Burks will be active again this Sunday versus Detroit.

items.h: Burks caught his only target for 14 yards during Sunday's 38-14 loss to the Seahawks.
items.s: The 2022 first-round pick from Arkansas was elevated from the Commanders' practice squad to the active roster to ensure depth at wide receiver, as both Terry McLaurin (quadriceps) and Noah Brown (groin) were sidelined Sunday. Burks played 33 offensive snaps and operated as Washington's No. 4 wideout, finishing as the team's fifth-leading receiver. He's likely to remain on the Commanders' active roster for the Week 10 matchup against the Lions, as McLaurin and Brown appear unlikely to return.

items.h: Burks was elevated from the Commanders' practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.s: Burks joined the Commanders' practice squad in mid-October after a lengthy recovery from a collarbone injury. With Terry McLaurin (quadriceps) ruled out, Burks has the chance to be active for the first time since Week 6 of the 2024 campaign.

items.h: Burks signed with Washington's practice squad Thursday.
items.s: Burks may need some time to learn the playbook, but he has a chance to be elevated and contribute right away Sunday against the Cowboys, as the Commanders may be severely shorthanded at wide receiver. Noah Brown (groin) is on injured reserve, and there are serious doubts about whether either of Terry McLaurin (quadriceps) or Deebo Samuel (heel) will be available. Burks had just 34 receiving yards in five games for the Titans last season.

items.h: Burks is expected to sign with the Commanders' practice squad, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Burks visited with both the Broncos and Commanders this past week, and the 2022 first-rounder appears to have chosen to join Washington as his next destination. Burks could be elevated to the active roster ahead of Sunday's NFC East tilt against the Cowboys, as the Commanders might be without Terry McLaurin (quadriceps) and Deebo Samuel (heel), while Noah Brown (groin) is on injured reserve. Burks has accumulated 53 catches (on 92 targets) for 699 yards and one touchdown over 27 regular-season games across his NFL career.

items.h: Burks visited the Broncos on Tuesday and plans to visit the Commanders on Wednesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Burks suffered a broken collarbone in July and was on the Titans' injured-reserve list before he was waived last week. Burks has a first-round draft pick pedigree but failed to live up to the billing in Tennessee. A change of scenery would do him well, and he appears to have plenty of interest as a reclamation project.

items.h: Tennessee waived Burks (collarbone) on Tuesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.s: Unless he's claimed off waivers, Burks will be eligible to sign with a new team once he's fully healthy after he spent the first five games of the season on the Titans' injured reserve list while on the mend from a fractured collarbone suffered during training camp. The No. 18 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, Burks was unable to carve out a meaningful role over his three-plus seasons in Tennessee. In 27 career games, the 25-year-old wideout tallied 53 receptions for 699 yards and one touchdown.

items.h: Burks (collarbone) was cleared for all football activities Monday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: The problem for Burks is he's currently on season-ending injured reserve with the Titans after he was placed on IR prior to roster cutdowns back in August. If he's going to play this season, the Titans will need to cut him and allow him to seek an opportunity elsewhere. It's unclear if those discussions have taken place, but a change of scenery would likely be best for Burks at this point in his career.

items.h: Burks (collarbone) reverted to the Titans' injured reserve Tuesday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Burks broke his right collarbone while making a diving catch at Saturday's practice. He'll be required to miss the entire 2025 season, unless he's waived with an injury settlement. Through three NFL campaigns, the 2022 first-round pick has compiled a disappointing 53-699-1 line on 92 targets in 27 regular-season games, including just four catches for 34 yards and no TDs in five contests last year.

items.h: The Titans waived Burks (collarbone) with an injury designation Monday, Jim Wyatt of the team's official site reports.
items.s: Burks suffered a broken collarbone in practice last week, and he'll now head to waivers after the Titans signed fellow WR Ramel Keyton in a corresponding move. If Burks clears waivers, he'll be placed on injured reserve, where he could then be cut with an injury settlement at a later date. Since being taken with the 18th overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, Burks has amassed a career receiving line of 53-699-1 on 92 targets across 27 regular-season contests. He's been neither healthy nor productive in Tennessee.

items.h: Burks fractured his collarbone during Saturday's practice, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.s: Burks made an incredible diving catch during Saturday's practice but came up holding his right shoulder before heading to the locker room. The 2022 first-round pick has struggled with injuries throughout his young career, as he suffered a torn ACL last season and has played only 27 regular-season games through three campaigns. It's unclear when he will return, but he's expected to at least miss the beginning of the season. This opens the door for Van Jefferson and rookies Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor to secure the No. 3 wide receiver role in the meantime.

items.h: Burks (shoulder/knee) exited Saturday's practice after making a diving one-handed catch, Paul Kuharsky of PaulKuharsky.com reports.
items.s: Burks has been practicing for a couple days now after his 2024 campaign was cut short due to a torn ACL. He beat a cornerback deep during Saturday's practice and made a phenomenal catch but came up holding his shoulder before heading to the locker room. Burks is vying for a starting wide receiver job during training camp, so any missed time will be detrimental.

items.h: Cameron Ward expressed optimism that Burks (knee) will be one of the Titans' top receivers in 2025, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
items.s: Burks has had a difficult start to his NFL career due to a combination of poor performance and injury. He's recovering from a torn ACL heading into his fourth campaign but has been practicing at the start of training camp, which should be a positive indication of his availability come the regular season. The Titans drafted Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor and also signed Van Jefferson and Tyler Lockett this offseason, giving Burks increased competition for targets.

items.h: Burks (knee) is expected to be ready for training camp, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: Burks, who is bouncing back from an ACL tear that he suffered Week 6 of the 2024 season, was only able to take part in individual periods of practice during OTAs and minicamp, but it looks like he'll be ready for more work in training camp. Once he's at or close to 100 percent, the 2022 first-rounder will have an opportunity to compete for slotting in a Tennessee wideout corps that is led by Calvin Ridley but unsettled beyond that.

items.h: Titans coach Brian Callahan said Wednesday that Burks (knee) is at about 80 percent strength and may be ready for Week 1, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: The 2022 first-round pick is finishing up his rehab from the ACL tear he suffered Week 6 last year, with a shot to be ready for the start of the final season of his rookie contract. Burks has averaged 2.0 catches for 25.9 yards in 27 career games, with just one touchdown among his 53 receptions, providing minimal reason for hope that he can live up to his draft status. He at least has some chance to earn playing time in Tennessee, where WR roles appear open for competition behind Calvin Ridley.

items.h: Burks (knee) practiced in a limited capacity during OTAs on Wednesday, John Glennon of NashvillePost.com reports.
items.s: It's an encouraging sign to see Burks working with the team as he heals from the ACL damage he incurred in Week 6 of the 2024 season. Per Terry McCormick of TitanInsider.com, coach Brian Callahan said Wednesday that while Burks isn't fully back, he'll be involved in practice as he progresses in his recovery. Once he's fully healthy, Tennessee hopes Burks will be able to compete for targets that don't go to Calvin Ridley with veteran wideouts Tyler Lockett and Van Jefferson, as well as rookies Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor.
